purpose: This medication is used to prevent pregnancy. It may also be prescribed to help with acne in women who want birth control at the same time. Some doctors also use it to help regulate periods or reduce painful menstrual cramps.
how_it_works: This pill contains two hormones — estrogen and progestin — that work together to prevent pregnancy in a few ways. First, they stop your ovaries from releasing an egg each month. They also thicken the mucus in your cervix so sperm has a harder time getting through, and they thin the lining of your uterus so a fertilized egg is less likely to attach.
common_side_effects: Nausea, headaches, breast tenderness or swelling, spotting or light bleeding between periods especially in the first few months, mood changes, decreased sex drive, and bloating. These often get better after the first 2-3 months.
warnings: Do not smoke while taking this pill, especially if you are over 35 — it seriously raises your risk of blood clots, stroke, and heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver problems, or breast cancer. This pill does NOT protect you from sexually transmitted infections. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you have severe chest pain, sudden vision changes, severe headache, or leg pain or swelling.
typical_dosing: You take one pill by mouth every day at the same time each day. Most packs have 28 pills — 21 active hormone pills and 7 reminder pills (or placebo pills). You start a new pack right after finishing the old one with no breaks. Taking it at the same time every day helps it work best and reduces side effects like nausea.
